claim: one consistent read per silo per run

claim: bounded-memory batched sync
status: BUILT 2026-10-13: the source is streamed (iter_all_rows: SQLite fetchmany, SQLAlchemy stream_results inside R4's held snapshot) straight into bronze as Arrow batches; bronze is read back as Arrow and cleaned 50,000 rows at a time (transform_batches, merged to the unbatched result); the changelog diff compares Arrow columns and builds dicts only for changed rows (diff_snapshot_tables, checked against diff_snapshots on randomised snapshots). claim: enforced retention and orphan-file cleanup
status: ORPHAN CLEANUP BUILT; RETENTION WAS ALREADY ENFORCED. Expiry (bronze, silver and gold each expire their own snapshots, with controls) unreferences files, and pyiceberg has nothing that deletes them (#3361), so the warehouse grew a file per table per sync for ever -- integrity.py measured it and check_mirror reported it. python -m scripts.remove_orphan_files is Iceberg's own remove_orphan_files for a local warehouse, with its two safeguards taken whole: only files older than a margin (72 h, Iceberg's three-day default -- a file a write has not yet committed is unreferenced too), and only files NO snapshot in the history references, so every retained snapshot and every published-N tag keeps its files. Plus this project's: it holds the sync lock, and it is a dry run unless given --write. Object-storage warehouses are refused: their lifecycle rules are the tool there. The audit row's M1 dependency could not be found in this checklist or the docs.

claim: an erasure (right-to-be-forgotten) workflow
status: EXTENDED 2026-10-14 to the owner's answer: every store but the audit log forgets -- frozen sets (members and criteria naming them), the write log (batches keep their other sub-writes, descriptions replaced), waiting writes (withdrawn; audited by write id and proposer only), paused questions (asker told generically) answer notifications (matched by the subjects now recorded with them), and merge proposals naming them with their decisions. core/mirror/erasure.forget_beyond_the_mirror serves erase and restore alike; audit stage `erasure` holds counts per type, no id. Gap: answer notifications written before subjects were recorded cannot be matched. || BUILT TO THE OWNER'S THREE DECISIONS (2026-10-12). (1) EVERYWHERE, REWRITTEN: python -m scripts.erase Type id --reason ... --write records the keys, rewrites every mirror table holding them (bronze, silver, changelog, quarantine, gold, gold_history, gold_conflicts -- mapped from the ontology's own storages and links, so a person is the object AND everything linking to it), drops every older tag and snapshot, and deletes the files outright; tested by opening every Parquet file in the warehouse and finding the person in none while an untouched customer remains. (2) SUPPRESSED UNTIL THE SOURCE CATCHES UP: every sync drops their rows on the way in and reports how many erased keys a source still returns; the register records when it stops. (3) RE-APPLIED ON RESTORE: the register is backed up, a restore keeps the NEWER register (it only grows) and marks every erasure unpurged, and the server refuses to start until a sync has applied them. THE REGISTER HOLDS NO ID: salted hashes, the salt kept inside it so a restore brings both back. Cannot erase the SOURCE, which Elysium only reads; it says what the source still holds. || 2026-10-14, OWNER: notes and memories about an erased object are deleted by the erasure and by a restore that would bring them back (ArtifactStore.forget_notes_about / forget_erased_notes; test_erasure.py::TestWhatPeopleWroteAboutThem, two controls).

claim: value kinds and per-value enrichment provenance
status: VALUE KIND BUILT 2026-10-15: an enriched field is `inferred` in visible_schema ("inferred from subject"), in the data contract's transformLogic, and marked on every value the UI shows. || SURVEYED IN FULL AND PARTLY BUILT, and the survey is the useful half: NO VALUE-KIND VOCABULARY EXISTS ANYWHERE. The complete set of field attributes the code reads is cardinality, column, constraints, data_type, decimal_places, on_violation, prefer, readable, required, standardise, status, storage, survivorship, target, timezone, type, via_*, visibility -- not one of them epistemic. `type` is structural (data or link), `data_type` is representational, and `status` is a SCHEMA lifecycle label (active/experimental/deprecated) that is defaulted in by visible_schema and declared in no fixture. Zero hits for `confidence` across core/, api/, templates/, ui/. AND THERE IS NOTHING TO ATTRIBUTE YET: no enrichment or derivation pipeline exists. standardise.py is the only thing that changes a value and is meaning-preserving by charter ('every rule declared, never inferred'); core/functions/ is agent tooling that persists nothing; reverse links are the only computed property and are computed from structure. Inference exists only for identity and only as proposals that a person approves. PER-VALUE PROVENANCE: one slice built. Everything the lake records about origin is per ROW -- `_silo`/`_source_table` name one source for a whole object, `_fused_from` names every contributing storage without saying which contributed what, and fusion.py says so in those words -- EXCEPT the gold_conflicts table, which is per field, per source, and had no reader: a repo-wide search found the writer, the namespace constant and two assertions in test_survivorship.py. survivorship.py's own docstring promised what it could not deliver -- 'deleting losing values destroys trust. A person asking why the golden record says Leeds needs to see that the CRM said Hull and was outranked' -- while the losers went to a table nobody could read, which is the bin with extra steps. Now readable: core/mirror/gold_conflicts.py, GET /objects/{type}/{id}/conflicts gated as /provenance is plus object visibility plus per-field read grants on the values, and a section on the object hub beside the lineage. AND IT FOUND TWO DEAD ROUTES ON THE WAY: /provenance and /published-history both looked for a `_catalog` attribute on one of the mediator's adapters, which GoldConnector does not have (it holds its catalog inside the reader it delegates to) -- and GOLD-9 made reads gold-only, so GoldConnector is the only adapter there is. Both have answered 'nothing recorded' on every real deployment since, and their tests passed because they guarded assertions with `if body is not None`. Fixed with a public `catalog` on both adapters and one helper, plus the assertion that was missing. PER-FIELD ATTRIBUTION BUILT 2026-10-12, as the owner chose: every fused gold row carries `_field_sources`, {field: source} for each non-null value, written by both fusion paths (the GOLD-5 join and GOLD-6 survivorship) -- the winner for every field, not only where sources disagreed. Served as `field_sources` on /provenance, MAC-checked and filtered to readable fields (the row's four opaque identifiers keep the ungated decision /conflicts records), and shown on the object hub as 'Which source supplied each value', with the silo relabelled 'Primary silo' on a fused object. The two R67 substitutions were closed by R67a/R67b. WHAT REMAINS FOR R38: the value-kind vocabulary (nothing to attribute until an enrichment pipeline exists) and per-property timestamps (declined in survivorship.py for want of one).

Graph metrics do not exist at all. BUT: search_object records the scan ceiling only if given an outcome, and count_objects and aggregate_by_field both called it without one -- so on a via_field type, where the 10,000-row budget is spent on candidates from every compartment, a count or a facet count came back SHORT with nothing in the response saying so. Never a leak (every id still passes check_access, so the error is always downward) but a wrong number reported as a right one, and the same class as the three silent-loss bugs fixed earlier in this series. Outcome now threaded through both methods, carried on CountResponse and AggregateResponse, and surfaced per field in Facets and per chart in ChartsPanel. THE AGENT PATH IS STILL UNREPORTED -- see R64.

Swept every layer and read the code rather than the names. field_types.coerce returns None for None and RAISES on anything unparseable -- no default, no fallback-to-string, and it refuses NaN, infinity, over-precise decimals and timezone guessing rather than rounding. transform.py keeps the RAW value on a coercion failure and names the column in a drift report, with a comment saying why: substituting would destroy the evidence. Aggregates EXCLUDE null group values and null field values before grouping, so sum([]) and avg([]) are structurally unreachable and no null is ever counted as zero. The UI's single renderer refuses the falsy bug explicitly -- zero and false are left alone, null renders as an em dash. (3) matching.py read Splink's three-valued gamma as two: -1 means the pair could not be compared because a value was null, and bool(gamma > 0) folded that into 'differ' -- presenting a null as evidence against a match, to a human deciding whether two records are the same person.
